counterevidence_considered.description: Against my no-issue verdict: a screening step did remove 8 of 40 planned units and the reported denominator is the retained 32, which superficially matches the issue-class pattern. This does not demonstrate the issue because both the task and the report define the scientific target as exactly that retained subset, so the denominator matches the declared domain.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- Planned nest boxes: 40
- Retained after screening (complete monitoring record): 32
- Removed by screening (incomplete monitoring record): 8

evidence.description: The governing task explicitly declares the retained post-screening subset as the scientific target, so a retained-subset denominator is the correct domain here, not a mismatch.

source_refs.quoted_text: Report one occurrence rate whose scientific target is explicitly the retained post-screening subset of observation units, using the planned-unit accounting supplied with this workflow.

evidence.description: The selected result is computed on and explicitly attributed to the retained subset (12/32 = 37.50%), with the claim scoped to that subset.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Among the 32 retained nest boxes, 12 showed barn owl occupancy: 12/32 = 37.50% of the retained post-screening subset.

evidence.description: The report's scope note affirmatively disclaims any claim about the removed boxes or the complete planned set, so the retained-subset rate is not projected onto the complete domain.
evidence.observed_value: no claim about 8 removed or 40 planned

source_refs.quoted_text:
The scientific target of this analysis is exclusively the retained subset of
32 nest boxes that passed screening. No occupancy claim is made about
the 8 removed boxes or about the complete planned set of 40 boxes.

evidence.description: Independent recount of inputs/data.csv confirms the accounting: 40 rows, 8 with monitoring_complete=no (B05, B11, B17, B22, B28, B33, B37, B40), 32 retained, and 12 retained rows with owl_pair_present=yes, matching 12/32 = 37.50%.

source_refs.quoted_text:
planned = len(rows)
retained_rows = [r for r in rows if r["monitoring_complete"] == "yes"]
retained = len(retained_rows)
removed = planned - retained
events = sum(1 for r in retained_rows if r["owl_pair_present"] == "yes")

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the no-issue verdict by searching the report for any sentence that extends the 37.50% rate to the 40 planned boxes or the 8 removed boxes: the title, study design, accounting, selected result, and scope note were each checked, and every claim is bounded to the 32 retained boxes, with the scope note explicitly disclaiming the complete planned set. I also verified the arithmetic and screening logic against inputs/data.csv (32 retained, 12 events) to confirm the denominator is genuinely the retained subset as declared, not a mislabeled complete-set count. No projection of the subset rate onto the complete domain exists in the visible files.
